$comment: The read that makes inbound email usable. Resend's email.received webhook carries metadata only -- "Webhooks do not include the email body, headers, or attachments" -- so the trigger names this action in its `then` block and runs it first. Read from https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/emails/retrieve-received-email, checked 2026-09-15.
title: Get received email
description: Read a received email in full: its bodies, its headers and the list of its attachments.

config.label: Email ID
config.description: The received email's id -- `data.email_id` on an email.received delivery. Not the message_id: that is the RFC 5322 header, which Resend does not look up by.

outputShape.description: Which estate this ran against. Resend has no sandbox, so: fake or live.
The connection id that was used.
The HTML body, when the email carried one.
How inline images are referenced in `html`: data_uri or cid.
The plain-text body. NULL when the email carried only HTML -- branch on it before reading.
The email's headers as a map, lower-cased names (from, return-path, mime-version, …).
Addresses the email was forwarded for, when it reached Resend through a forward.
The RFC 5322 Message-ID, angle brackets included. Dedupe across providers on this.
A signed URL for the raw MIME message. Expires -- see raw.expires_at. NULL when Resend kept no raw copy.
ISO 8601 expiry of raw.download_url, about an hour after the read.
The attachments' METADATA -- id, filename, content_type, content_disposition, content_id, size -- never the bytes. attachment_get turns an id into a download URL.
